paper: Intra-Session recurrence in intradialytic hypotension prediction: evaluation implications and recurrence-aware modeling
authors_short: Kim S, Ryu J, Kim S, Kim SH
problem: Real-time intradialytic hypotension (IDH) prediction; effect of initial vs recurrent IDH within a session on evaluation
method: ConvMixer, TCN, LSTM-attention vs a rule-based naive baseline predicting IDH from prior occurrence; recurrence-aware features and loss weighting; adversarial training
claimed_novelty: Aggregated evaluation overestimates performance; naive prior-occurrence baseline reaches AUROC 0.798 without training; recurrence-aware modelling adds up to 8.0 points AUROC; recommends recurrence-aware evaluation protocols
what_they_do_not_do: Dialysis-session IDH (SBP-based, ~4-h sessions), not ICU/OR MAP<65; no burden-matched (alarms per patient-hour) comparison with a current-pressure alarm; recurrence information is used to raise accuracy rather than to allocate separate alarm budgets
how_ours_differs: Closest prior art to C1/C2 (same initial-vs-recurrent split and naive-prior-occurrence argument, in dialysis); we transfer it to ICU/OR MAP<65 with 1-min numerics, a current-MAP baseline at fixed alarms per patient-hour, a 6-h history definition, and state-specific alarm budgets (C3) rather than recurrence-aware features.

paper: Prediction of hypotension events with physiologic vital sign signatures in the intensive care unit
authors_short: Yoon JH, Jeanselme V, Dubrawski A, et al.
problem: Predict first hypotension event in ICU 15-60 min ahead
method: Random forest on 30-min windows of minute-level vitals; stacked RF alert model with lockout
data: MIMIC-III minute vitals (1580 hypotensive vs 2279 control stays)
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.93 at 15 min; alert system yields 0.79 alerts/subject/hour at 92.4% sensitivity
what_they_do_not_do: Predicts only the initial hypotension event per ICU stay with a hypotensive vs control cohort; does not evaluate recurrent events or compare against a current-MAP alarm at matched alarm burden.
how_ours_differs: Its first-event design corresponds to our new-onset stratum; we evaluate new-onset and recurrent events from the same deployed model on all time points and show that pooled evaluation can mask a new-onset deficit relative to current MAP.

paper: Pharmacokinetic State Space Models for Unbiased Prediction of Haemodynamic Collapse
authors_short: Nagaraj R, Chindula S, Das B
venue: arXiv preprint / Lecture Notes in Computer Science
problem: IOH prediction incorporating anaesthetic drug infusion history
method: Mamba state-space deep network with propofol/remifentanil effect-site concentrations; lead-gap filtering
data: Intraoperative data (VitalDB-type; abstract does not name it: UNVERIFIED)
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.736; shows unfiltered training learns to detect ongoing rather than future hypotension
what_they_do_not_do: Shows that training without lead-gap filtering makes models detect ongoing hypotension, but does not stratify by prior-episode history or match alarm burden.
how_ours_differs: Closest IOH analogue of our shortcut finding: they show contamination by ongoing hypotension; we show that even with lead-gap filtering, gains concentrate in patients with recent (but not ongoing) hypotension.
verified_via: arXiv API (arXiv id lookup); chapter DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-35387-0_22 also confirmed via Crossref (LNCS, Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare, 2026); checked 2026-11-23

paper: Performance of the Hypotension Prediction Index May Be Overestimated Due to Selection Bias
authors_short: Enevoldsen J, Vistisen ST
problem: Critique of HPI training/validation data selection
method: Analytical critique with simulated data
claimed_novelty: Shows that HPI's sampling makes MAP<75 always predict hypotension, inflating apparent performance
what_they_do_not_do: Identifies selection bias in HPI training/validation data; does not stratify by prior-hypotension history.
how_ours_differs: We extend the evaluation-bias critique from sample selection to event-history mixture: even with unbiased sampling, pooled metrics are dominated by recurrent events.

paper: Hypotension Prediction Index Is Equally Effective in Predicting Intraoperative Hypotension during Noncardiac Surgery Compared to a Mean Arterial Pressure Threshold: A Prospective Observational Study
authors_short: Mulder MP, Harmannij-Markusse M, Fresiello L, et al.
problem: Compare HPI with MAP-based predictors
method: Prospective observational; alarm agreement and ROC of HPI vs MAP, linearly extrapolated MAP, delta MAP
claimed_novelty: HPI AUROC 0.89 vs MAP 0.88; MAP 72-73 mmHg threshold matches HPI alarms
what_they_do_not_do: Shows HPI ~ MAP 72-73 mmHg alarm overall; abstract reports no new-onset vs recurrent split.
how_ours_differs: Directly supports our current-MAP baseline; we add event-history stratification and matched-burden sensitivity for open ICU/OR models.

paper: The effect of selection bias on the performance of a deep learning-based intraoperative hypotension prediction model using real-world samples from a publicly available database
authors_short: Yang H-L, Celi LA, Lee H, et al.
problem: Quantify selection-bias effect on DL and MAP-only IOH models
method: Train/test DL vs MAP-only on biased vs unbiased sampling; alarms per hour and PPV
claimed_novelty: Unbiased testing: 18.1 alarms/h and PPV 0.068 vs 10.8/h and 0.937 biased; DL gain over MAP not clinically meaningful
what_they_do_not_do: Shows selection bias inflates PPV and that DL ~ MAP-only under unbiased sampling with alarms per hour; does not split events by prior hypotension.
how_ours_differs: Closest evaluation-protocol precedent (unbiased all-sample testing, alarms/h, MAP-only comparator); we add the new-onset vs recurrent split and show the residual DL advantage can be recurrent-only.

paper: Blood pressure history improves near-term hypotension prediction and reassessment prioritisation in sepsis
authors_short: Wang L, Zhu J, Zhou R, et al.
problem: Predict hypotension within 4 h after target pressure is reached in sepsis, using blood-pressure history
method: Gradient boosting with 24 pressure-history predictors, patient-level cross-fitting; chronological replay at matched prompt counts; target-trial emulation of norepinephrine reduction
data: 370,447 windows from 22,485 patients in MIMIC-IV, eICU and SICdb
claimed_novelty: Pressure history improves AUROC over current information and yields more pre-hypotensive captures at the same prompt count
what_they_do_not_do: 4-h horizon in vasopressor-treated sepsis; frames prior pressure history as a desirable predictor of recurrent hypotension; abstract does not report performance separately for patients without vs with recent hypotension
how_ours_differs: Opposite emphasis to C1: they show history improves pooled prediction of (largely recurrent) hypotension at matched prompts, whereas we show that at 15 min and fixed alarms per patient-hour this gain is concentrated in recurrent events and absent for new-onset events.

paper: Hypotension During Vasopressor Infusion Occurs in Predictable Clusters: A Multicenter Analysis
authors_short: Horiguchi D, Shin S, Pepino JA, et al.
problem: Characterise ICU hypotension during vasopressor infusion and its predictability from MAP trends
method: Retrospective analysis of hypotension-clusters (>=10 min cumulative per 60 min); MAP trend extrapolation from 14 min of data
data: Three ICU cohorts (155, 66, 16 stays) incl. spinal cord injury
claimed_novelty: Most hypotension occurs in temporal clusters and is usually predictable from MAP-trend extrapolation (sensitivity 81-94%, PPV 51-73%)
what_they_do_not_do: Descriptive plus trend extrapolation; no trained ML model and no comparison of ML gains between first and recurrent events
how_ours_differs: Provides the physiological premise of C1 (ICU hypotension is clustered/recurrent); we quantify the consequence for evaluating trained models against current MAP at fixed burden.

paper: The dynamics of arterial pressure itself predict intraoperative hypotension beyond its current value: an interpretable additive model validated in 3,069 external patients under a selection-bias-resistant protocol
authors_short: Oyarzun R, Hernández-Hernández P
problem: Does MAP dynamics add information beyond current MAP for IOH under a selection-bias-resistant protocol?
method: Additive gradient boosting on current MAP, drift from 20-min baseline and rolling-variance growth; excludes 65-75 grey zone and samples already hypotensive; MAP-alone comparator
data: VitalDB (807 patients) development; MOVER (3,069 patients) pre-registered external validation
claimed_novelty: Pressure dynamics add AUROC +0.02-0.06 over MAP alone; advantage collapses (+0.007) when already-hypotensive samples are retained
what_they_do_not_do: Excludes samples already hypotensive but does not stratify by recent-but-resolved hypotension; AUROC rather than burden-matched event sensitivity
how_ours_differs: Shows that inclusion of already-hypotensive samples changes the ML-vs-MAP verdict; we go further by separating patients with a resolved episode in the prior 6 h, where pooled gains concentrate.

paper: Evaluation of Sepsis Prediction Models before Onset of Treatment
authors_short: Kamran F, Tjandra D, Heiler A, et al.
problem: Evaluate Epic Sepsis Model predictions made before clinical recognition/treatment
method: AUROC of ESM predictions restricted to before sepsis criteria and before treatment indicators (antibiotics, fluids, cultures, lactate)
claimed_novelty: AUROC falls from 0.62 to 0.47 when predictions after clinical recognition are excluded
what_they_do_not_do: Sepsis, not haemodynamics; conditions on clinician recognition rather than prior-event history; no burden-matched comparison
how_ours_differs: Same structural lesson in a different domain (models score well on patients already recognised); our analogue conditions on recent hypotension episodes and quantifies it at fixed alarms per patient-hour.

paper: Early prediction of circulatory failure in the intensive care unit using machine learning
authors_short: Hyland SL, Faltys M, Hüser M, et al.
problem: Early warning of circulatory failure in ICU patients
method: Gradient-boosted ML early-warning system integrating multi-organ measurements
data: High-resolution Bern ICU database (240 patient-years; HiRID) with external validation cohort
claimed_novelty: Detects 90% of circulatory-failure events (82% >2 h ahead), AUROC 0.94, with ~0.05 alarms per patient-hour, lower false-alarm rate than threshold systems
what_they_do_not_do: Abstract reports pooled event recall and alarms per patient-hour for a composite circulatory-failure label; no split of events by prior-episode history and no burden-matched comparison against a current-MAP alarm.
how_ours_differs: We adopt its alarms-per-patient-hour framing but split MAP<65 events into new-onset vs recurrent (episode in prior 6 h) and test whether a trained model's pooled advantage over a current-MAP alarm survives in the new-onset stratum.

paper: Prediction of an Acute Hypotensive Episode During an ICU Hospitalization With a Super Learner Machine-Learning Algorithm
authors_short: Cherifa M, Blet A, Chambaz A, et al.
problem: Predict acute hypotensive episodes (MAP<65 for >=5 min) 10 min ahead in ICU
method: Super Learner ensemble with Haar-wavelet features from HR, SpO2, ABP plus clinical covariates
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.93 (one random period per patient) / 0.89 (all periods); external validation
what_they_do_not_do: Although 72% of patients had at least one AHE, evaluation used one random period per patient (and all periods); abstract reports no split by whether an AHE occurred in the preceding hours.
how_ours_differs: We make that split explicit (new-onset vs recurrent within 6 h) and show it changes the verdict on ML vs current MAP, which neither of its evaluation schemes can reveal.

paper: Forecasting Hypotension during Vasopressor Infusion via Time Series Analysis
authors_short: Shin S, Reisner AT, Yapps B, et al.
problem: Forecast sustained hypotension during vasopressor infusion in ICU
method: Logistic regression and autoregressive (AR) time-series forecasting vs simple threshold detector
claimed_novelty: AR and LR models warn several minutes before sustained hypotension without more false alarms; AR flexible to any threshold
what_they_do_not_do: Compares AR/LR forecasting with a simple threshold detector during vasopressor infusion; abstract does not stratify events by prior hypotension or use matched alarm burden.
how_ours_differs: We extend the model-vs-threshold comparison by matching alarms per patient-hour and splitting events by recent-hypotension status, where the ranking can reverse.

paper: Towards actionable hypotension prediction -- predicting catecholamine therapy initiation in the intensive care unit
authors_short: Koebe R, Saibel N, Lopez Alcaraz JM, et al.
problem: Predict catecholamine initiation within 15 min in ICU
method: XGBoost with SHAP on 2-h MAP context statistics plus covariates
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.82 vs 0.69 for MAP<65 baseline; reframes target as treatment escalation
what_they_do_not_do: Reframes the target as catecholamine initiation; SHAP shows recent MAP and ongoing treatments dominate, but no analysis of whether gains concentrate in already-unstable patients.
how_ours_differs: Its SHAP finding (recent MAP and ongoing treatment dominate) is consistent with our state-shortcut hypothesis, which we test directly by stratifying MAP<65 events by prior-6-h hypotension at fixed burden.

paper: Machine-learning Algorithm to Predict Hypotension Based on High-fidelity Arterial Pressure Waveform Analysis
authors_short: Hatib F, Jian Z, Buddi S, et al.
problem: Predict intraoperative MAP<65 5-15 min ahead (Hypotension Prediction Index)
method: Logistic-type model on 3,022 arterial-waveform features per beat
data: 1,334 retrospective patients for training; 204-patient prospective external cohort
claimed_novelty: AUROC 0.95 at 15 min; sensitivity/specificity ~88%/87%
what_they_do_not_do: Case-control style training/validation selection; no stratification by prior hypotension and no matched-burden comparison with a current-MAP alarm.
how_ours_differs: We evaluate on all time points with a burden-matched current-MAP baseline and show where (recurrent events) apparent ML advantages arise.

paper: Towards reliable prediction of intraoperative hypotension: a cross-center evaluation of deep learning-based and MAP-derived methods
authors_short: Chaari N, Winski G, Hallbäck M, et al.
venue: Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing
problem: Assess reliability and cross-centre generalisation of IOH prediction vs MAP thresholds
method: Deep learning vs MAP threshold; 'Gray Zone' (65-75 mmHg) inclusion; standardised MAP difference between classes
claimed_novelty: Shows inflated performance stems from selection bias; asymmetric cross-centre generalisability
what_they_do_not_do: Addresses grey-zone (65-75 mmHg) selection bias and cross-centre asymmetry; does not stratify by prior-hypotension history.
how_ours_differs: Complementary bias axis: they control MAP separation at prediction time, we control recent event history, and both change the ML-vs-MAP verdict.

paper: Forecasting cumulative intraoperative hypotension burden: patient-disjoint evaluation of quantile boosting and alert policies
authors_short: Zhao Y
problem: Forecast next-15-min MAP deficit below 65 (burden) and separate forecast skill from alert performance
method: Quantile boosting, direct and residual-on-persistence, vs climatology and persistence; validation-selected alert thresholds
data: VitalDB numeric MAP (10-s medians), subject-disjoint splits
claimed_novelty: Residual quantile boosting beats persistence; shows warning performance depends on alert rule
what_they_do_not_do: Separates burden-forecast skill from warning-policy performance against persistence baselines; no new-onset vs recurrent stratification.
how_ours_differs: Shares our emphasis on alert-policy evaluation against persistence/current-MAP baselines; we add the prior-event stratification and state-specific alarm budgets.

paper: Ability of an Arterial Waveform Analysis-Derived Hypotension Prediction Index to Predict Future Hypotensive Events in Surgical Patients
authors_short: Davies SJ, Vistisen ST, Jian Z, et al.
problem: Validate HPI vs other haemodynamic variables
method: Retrospective ROC analysis of HPI and haemodynamic variables
claimed_novelty: HPI AUROC 0.93/0.90/0.88 at 5/10/15 min, reportedly superior to MAP
what_they_do_not_do: Reports HPI superior to MAP in pooled backward-selected data; no prior-event stratification.
how_ours_differs: We show that model-vs-MAP comparisons need event-history stratification and matched burden to be interpretable.

paper: Is Continuous Intraoperative Monitoring of Mean Arterial Pressure as Good as the Hypotension Prediction Index Algorithm?: Research Letter
authors_short: Mulder MP, Harmannij-Markusse M, Donker DW, et al.
problem: Compare HPI signal and alarms with MAP
method: Cross-correlation of HPI and MAP; alarm concordance
data: 33 high-risk noncardiac surgery patients, unselected 20-s data
claimed_novelty: HPI strongly mirrors MAP in unselected data
what_they_do_not_do: Shows HPI closely mirrors MAP in unselected data; no prior-event stratification.
how_ours_differs: We add the observation that what a model adds beyond MAP can be concentrated in recurrent events.

paper: Comparison of Differences in Cohort (Forward) and Case Control (Backward) Methodologic Approaches for Validation of the Hypotension Prediction Index
authors_short: Davies SJ, Sessler DI, Jian Z, et al.
problem: Quantify impact of forward vs backward validation on HPI
method: Re-analysis of pooled studies with both methodologies
claimed_novelty: HPI AUC remains ~0.92 in forward analysis; MAP itself has similar AUC (~0.93)
what_they_do_not_do: Compares forward vs backward validation; no prior-event stratification.
how_ours_differs: We adopt forward (all-time-point) evaluation and additionally split by event history.

paper: Comparing the Hypotension Prediction Index to Mean Arterial Pressure and Linear Extrapolated Mean Arterial Pressure for the Prediction of Intraoperative Hypotension: A Secondary Analysis
authors_short: Massari D, de Keijzer IN, Vos JJ
problem: Head-to-head HPI vs MAP vs linearly extrapolated MAP
method: Secondary analysis of a mixed-methods cohort
claimed_novelty: HPI not superior to MAP or extrapolated MAP
what_they_do_not_do: HPI vs MAP vs extrapolated MAP; no stratification by prior hypotension.
how_ours_differs: We add event-history stratification and fixed-burden comparison to the MAP-baseline literature.

paper: The hypotension prediction index versus mean arterial pressure in predicting intraoperative hypotension: A clinical perspective
authors_short: Rellum SR, Noteboom SH, van der Ster BJP, et al.
problem: Clinical comparison of HPI vs MAP alert thresholds
method: Time-to-event, PPV and missed events for HPI popups vs MAP 70-75 alerts
claimed_novelty: HPI gains <1 min lead time over MAP-70 alerts; MAP-75 lowers PPV
what_they_do_not_do: HPI vs MAP thresholds with PPV and lead time; no new-onset vs recurrent analysis.
how_ours_differs: Same baseline philosophy; our novelty is the prior-event stratification and state-specific budgets.

paper: Prediction of intraoperative hypotension from the linear extrapolation of mean arterial pressure
authors_short: Jacquet-Lagrèze M, Larue A, Guilherme E, et al.
problem: Test linearly extrapolated MAP (LepMAP) for IOH prediction
method: Linear extrapolation of minute MAP vs delta MAP; ROC
claimed_novelty: LepMAP AUC 0.87/0.81/0.69 at 1/2/5 min, far better than delta MAP
what_they_do_not_do: Linear extrapolation of MAP as a predictor; no event-history stratification.
how_ours_differs: We use current/extrapolated MAP as baselines and ask which events trained models beat them on.

paper: Predicting arterial pressure without prejudice: towards effective hypotension prediction models
authors_short: Vistisen ST, Elbers P
problem: Editorial on selection bias in hypotension prediction
method: Commentary on Yang et al.
claimed_novelty: Argues unbiased training lets models learn only modestly beyond current BP; bias inflates PPV
what_they_do_not_do: Editorial on selection bias; no empirical stratification.
how_ours_differs: We provide one concrete mechanism behind the 'modest gain beyond current BP' they anticipate: recent-hypotension history.

paper: Why the C-statistic is not informative to evaluate early warning scores and what metrics to use
authors_short: Romero-Brufau S, Huddleston JM, Escobar GJ, et al.
problem: Metrics for early warning scores
method: Methodological commentary
claimed_novelty: Recommends sensitivity plus PPV/number-needed-to-evaluate or alert rate instead of AUROC
what_they_do_not_do: Recommends sensitivity plus alert rate instead of C-statistic; no stratification by event history.
how_ours_differs: We follow its metric recommendation and add stratification by new-onset vs recurrent events.

paper: Continuous Evaluation Frameworks for Retrospective Evaluation of Clinical Machine Learning Models
authors_short: Natarajan A, Chang Y, McLaverty BP, et al.
problem: Evaluate continuously running clinical ML models
method: Zone-based, PAMC-curve-based and notification-based frameworks
data: Sepsis model predictions on two public datasets
claimed_novelty: Captures model behaviour over time beyond single-time-point AUROC
what_they_do_not_do: Proposes continuous (zone/AMOC/notification) evaluation frameworks for sepsis models; no stratification by prior-event history.
how_ours_differs: Complementary continuous-evaluation framework; ours adds an event-history axis and fixed-burden comparison against a physiological baseline.

paper: Compact clinical features capturing organ history for dynamic prediction of organ deterioration in sepsis
authors_short: Wang L, Song J, Vereshchako M, et al.
problem: Six-hour organ deterioration prediction in sepsis using organ-history features
method: 175-variable model; comparison of 3,072 combinations of 12 historical sources at fixed alert spacing and 0.50 alerts per patient
data: 19,690 adults with sepsis in MIMIC-IV, eICU, CareVue, SICdb; 1,661 pancreatitis patients
claimed_novelty: History sources capture 30-82% more events than current information at fixed alert rate
what_they_do_not_do: Organ-deterioration endpoint; history is treated as signal to exploit; no split of events by prior-event status
how_ours_differs: Uses a fixed-alert-rate comparison like C2 but treats history as uniformly beneficial; we ask for which patients (no recent event vs recent event) history-driven gains occur.

paper: Extrapolation of MAP trends predicts hypotension and vasopressor up-titration in the ICU.
authors_short: Kehoe IE, Pepino JA, Hahn JO, et al.
problem: Prospective pilot of a MAP-trend CDSS predicting 15-min hypotension and vasopressor up-titration in ICU
method: Real-time MAP trend extrapolation with probability cone; no predictions during active hypotension; diagnostic statistics per 15-min bin
claimed_novelty: All hypotension-clusters identified during early 'flickering' hypotension; 44% predicted before any hypotension; PPV 58%
what_they_do_not_do: Very small pilot; separates prediction before any hypotension vs during flickering descriptively but compares no trained ML model and uses no alarm-budget matching
how_ours_differs: Its 'before any hypotension' vs 'during flickering' distinction parallels our new-onset vs recurrent split; we test it at scale for trained models vs current MAP with burden matching across three open cohorts.

paper: Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Acute Hypotensive Events in Intensive Care Unit Patients
authors_short: Nakanishi T, Tsuji T, Tamura T, et al.
problem: Predict all acute hypotensive events (MAP<60 for 5 of 10 min) in the first ICU week
method: Logistic regression, LightGBM, LSTM on vital-sign statistics; lockout-based alert frequency
claimed_novelty: LSTM with BP-only features AUROC 0.843 with consistent external performance
what_they_do_not_do: Discussion attributes its lower AUROC vs Yoon et al. to targeting recurrent events rather than only the first event, but does not stratify evaluation by first vs recurrent events
how_ours_differs: Explicitly notes the first-event vs all-events design difference (full text); we measure that difference within one model and show its direction at fixed burden.

paper: Open-Source Neural Network vs. Simple Hemodynamic Rules for Intraoperative Hypotension Prediction
authors_short: Shannon K, Meyer C, Patel B, Menon AA
problem: Open-source CNN vs simple MAP rules for IOH across four definitions
method: CNN on MAP time series vs MAP threshold rule and 3-feature trend logistic regression; discrimination, calibration, net benefit, alert burden, lead time
claimed_novelty: CNN offered no advantage over a one-line MAP rule for absolute-threshold IOH; only baseline-aware model works for relative-drop definition
what_they_do_not_do: Pooled evaluation; no stratification by prior hypotension
how_ours_differs: Concordant 'ML ~ MAP rule' result with alert burden reported; we explain where residual gains arise (recurrent events) and propose state-specific budgets.

paper: Patient Versus Prediction-Level Evaluation of a Dynamic Clinical Prediction Model of Sepsis
authors_short: Tuttle M, Maas CCHM, An J, et al.
problem: Patient-level vs prediction-level evaluation of a dynamic sepsis model (ESMv2)
method: Retrospective cohort comparing maximum-prediction (patient-level) with every-prediction (prediction-level) analyses
claimed_novelty: Patient-level AUC 0.86 vs prediction-level 0.62; PPV 14.5% vs 4%
what_they_do_not_do: Evaluation-granularity bias only; no prior-event stratification
how_ours_differs: Another evaluation-design bias for dynamic models; ours is the event-history mixture bias.

paper: Machine learning for patient risk stratification: standing on, or looking over, the shoulders of clinicians?
authors_short: Beaulieu-Jones BK, Yuan W, Brat GA, et al.
problem: Do EHR risk models learn clinicians' actions rather than physiology?
method: Deep learning on clinician-initiated administrative data only (demographics, admission info, day-1 charges)
claimed_novelty: Clinician-action-only models approach full-EHR benchmarks; proposes these as benchmarks to exceed
what_they_do_not_do: Outcome-level (mortality, LOS, readmission) risk; no short-horizon alarms or event-history stratification
how_ours_differs: Conceptual precedent for 'the model predicts what is already known'; our 'already known' signal is recent hypotension, and we quantify it per event stratum.

paper: Hypotension Prediction Index versus Mean Arterial Pressure Alarm for Preventing Intraoperative Hypotension in Elective Noncardiac Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors_short: Florax AA, Mulder MP, van Ieperen RP, et al.
problem: RCT: MAP<72 mmHg alarm vs HPI>85 alarm for preventing IOH
method: Single-centre blinded noninferiority RCT
claimed_novelty: A 72 mmHg MAP alarm was noninferior to HPI in AUT<65 mmHg
what_they_do_not_do: Interventional comparison; no stratification of events by prior hypotension
how_ours_differs: Prospective support for a current-MAP baseline; we add retrospective evidence on which event types a trained model can beat it on.

paper: Ability of the hypotension prediction index to predict hypotension in patients with septic shock in the intensive care unit
authors_short: Khwannimit B, Sathaporn N, Vattanavanit V
problem: HPI performance for hypotension in ICU septic shock
method: Prospective; positive samples 5-15 min before events; non-events MAP>75 or >=65
data: 30 septic shock patients, 645 events (median 14.5 events per patient)
claimed_novelty: HPI AUC 0.92-0.95, but similar to current MAP once 65-75 mmHg samples count as non-events
what_they_do_not_do: Many recurrent events per patient pooled; no split by prior-event history
how_ours_differs: Shows ICU hypotension is highly recurrent (median 14.5 events/patient) and that HPI ~ MAP under fairer sampling; we stratify such recurrent events explicitly.

paper: Performance of a machine-learning algorithm to predict hypotension in mechanically ventilated patients with COVID-19 admitted to the intensive care unit: a cohort study
authors_short: van der Ven WH, Terwindt LE, Risvanoglu N, et al.
venue: Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing
problem: HPI performance in mechanically ventilated COVID-19 ICU patients
method: Threshold sweep of HPI; 20-min event windows
data: 41 ICU patients; median 21 hypotensive events per patient
claimed_novelty: HPI AUC 0.95 for MAP<65 within 20 min
what_they_do_not_do: Pooled evaluation of highly recurrent events; no comparison with current MAP at matched burden
how_ours_differs: An example of pooled ICU evaluation dominated by recurrent events (93% of patients had events, median 21 each), which our stratified protocol is designed to disentangle.

paper: Rigorous evaluation of five models for e‐diary‐only seizure forecasting: Retrospective and prospective datasets do not outperform the Napkin method
authors_short: Chang CY, Moss R, Westover MB, Goldenholz DM
problem: Do e-diary seizure forecasting models beat a moving-average (Napkin) baseline?
method: Five ML models vs moving-window average of recent seizure counts; AUPRC, AUROC, Brier
claimed_novelty: No model significantly outperformed the Napkin (recent-history average) method
what_they_do_not_do: 24-h seizure risk from diaries; no state-stratified evaluation
how_ours_differs: Cross-field analogue: a recent-event-history baseline matches trained models; we show the converse risk that trained models' gains are themselves recent-history effects.

paper: Prediction of First and Recurrent Falls in Parkinson's Disease
authors_short: Vizcarra JA, Hefter K, Duong MT, et al.
problem: Separate prediction of incident (first) and recurrent falls in Parkinson's disease
method: Separate incident and recurrent models with external validation
claimed_novelty: Distinct predictors and risk strata for incident vs recurrent falls
what_they_do_not_do: Annual horizon, no alarms or budgets
how_ours_differs: Analogue of C3's state-specific modelling (separate incident vs recurrent models) in a different domain and horizon; we add separate alarm budgets for minute-scale warnings.

paper: Development and prospective evaluation of a real-time deep learning model for inpatient hypoglycemia prediction
authors_short: Momenzadeh A, Cranney C, Chen DH, et al.
problem: Real-time inpatient hypoglycaemia prediction within 24 h
method: LSTM vs LR/DNN/XGBoost; SHAP; prospective daily validation
claimed_novelty: F1 0.30; SHAP top predictors include recent insulin and prior hypoglycaemia
what_they_do_not_do: No split of events into first vs recurrent hypoglycaemia
how_ours_differs: Prior-event features rank among top predictors in another threshold-crossing task; we test whether such features help on new-onset events.

paper: From Prediction to Practice: A Task-Aware Evaluation Framework for Blood Glucose Forecasting
authors_short: Namazi A, Shakeri H
problem: Task-aware evaluation of glucose forecasting for hypoglycaemia early warning and dosing
method: Event-level recall and false alarms per patient-day, sliced by clinical state (post-bolus); simulator-based interventional arm
